title: Christmas Eve
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Does Chloe come home. The strip walks to her house to find out, and draws the house instead.

panels.composition: Main street, Christmas Eve, rain, the hardware store lights all out this year. WOOD walking BARNABY. Four houses down: Chloe's.

image.prompt: a young man walking a small dog down a small-town main street on a rainy Christmas Eve, a hardware store with dead lights, a row of houses ahead, black and white

panels.composition: Chloe's house. A wreath. Lights inside. A car in the driveway with Washington plates — no. Oregon plates. Her parents' car.

image.prompt: a young man stopped on a wet sidewalk in front of a small house with a wreath and lit windows, a car with Oregon plates in the driveway, a dog sniffing the hedge
image.notes: Plates: OREGON. Not hers. Letter after if needed.

panels.composition: A silhouette in the window. Her mother. Not her.

image.prompt: close-up of a lit house window at night with a woman's silhouette that is clearly not a teenager

panels.composition: Wood on the sidewalk, drawing the house on the pad in the rain. Barnaby waiting. The strip's Christmas Eve is a drawing of a house she isn't in.

characters.pose: drawing the house in the rain

image.prompt: a young man standing on a rainy sidewalk at night drawing a lit house on a pad while a small dog waits at his feet, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The December fixture proper. She does not come home. The strip draws the house.
